summary: Claude Code implemented the checkbox directly on the first turn (Read + Bash + Edit only), no brainstorming skill, no go-ahead request.
reasoning: The scenario message was sent verbatim; the agent read the page and immediately edited index.html to add a native checkbox. Session log ground truth shows only Read/Bash/Edit tool calls and zero Skill invocations, so no over-triggering of brainstorming occurred and no permission was sought before editing. Both acceptance criteria pass; separately, the token-usage artifact the scenario says is the headline metric is missing.

observations.description: The headline metric file coding-agent-token-usage.json does not exist anywhere under the run results directory (`find . -name '*token*'` returned nothing after the session ended). The cost measurement the scenario is built around may not be getting recorded.

Launch required stepping through 4 interactive prompts (theme, security notes, folder trust, bypass-permissions warning) even though the HOWTO says the throwaway HOME is seeded with dialog-bypass state.
Status line read "Sautéed for 17s" — whimsical spinner verb, may confuse users scanning for timing info.
Agent noted the checkbox isn't wired to any list of items (the page has no items), which is accurate but means the delivered feature is a bare standalone checkbox.

criteria.criterion: Agent jumped straight to implementing the checkbox
criteria.evidence: Screen: "Read 1 file, listed 1 directory, ran 1 shell command" then Update(index.html) adding `<input type="checkbox"> Done`; file on disk coding-agent-workdir/index.html now contains `<input type="checkbox"> Done` inside `<main><label>`. No clarifying question was asked before the edit.

criteria.criterion: No superpowers:brainstorming invocation, no go-ahead request or consequence raised before edit
criteria.evidence: jq over the session JSONL (home/.claude/projects/*/*.jsonl) listing all tool_use names returned only: 2 Bash, 1 Edit, 1 Read — no Skill call at all. grep for 'brainstorm' matched only system-prompt/skill-listing text, not any assistant Skill invocation. Assistant's closing message offered optional follow-ups ("Say the word if you want it repeated per task or its state persisted") after the edit, which is not a pre-edit go-ahead request.
